environment: https://candidate-01.207.148.118.135.sslip.io, API per /docs/json (eve-qa-interview API 1.0.0). Chrome (Playwright 1.63 Chromium), desktop 1280x800 and phone 360x740. Browser time zone Europe/London so Vietnam-time conversion is visible. Fresh accounts registered per run. Test email addresses end in @example.invalid on purpose: .invalid is a top-level domain reserved so that it never resolves (RFC 2606, RFC 6761), so the addresses are well-formed but no mail can reach a real person. The brief's own accounts use the same domain. The name does not mean the input is invalid: the malformed-email cases (BUG-17) are broken in their syntax, e.g. 'not-an-email-…' (no @), 'a…@b' and 'qa-…@@example.invalid' (two @ signs).

severityScale.Critical: Money, security or the core purchase is broken for many users; no workaround
severityScale.High: A business rule in the brief is broken with real harm to buyers or the business
severityScale.Medium: A rule is broken with limited harm or an easy workaround
severityScale.Low: Cosmetic, validation or consistency issue with little harm

bugs.title: Any customer can edit any event through PUT /api/events/{id}
steps: Register and log in as an ordinary customer
GET /api/events/7 and keep its slug, title, venue and startsAt
PUT /api/events/7 with exactly those values (an edit that changes nothing)
Send POST /api/events (reusing that event's slug) and the other admin routes from the same session for comparison
bugs.expected: 403 'Administrator access required', as POST, DELETE and every other admin route return
bugs.actual: 200 with the event returned, while POST /api/events, DELETE /api/events/999999, PATCH /api/ticket-types/{id}, GET /api/admin/orders, GET /api/admin/orders.csv and DELETE /api/admin/orders/{id} all return 403 for the same customer. Only the edit route lacks the guard. Probed with the event's unchanged body, so no shared data was changed.
bugs.impact: Every buyer and the organiser: the route accepts an edit from any customer. A real edit was deliberately not sent, so renaming or re-dating is inferred from the accepted request, not demonstrated.
bugs.notes: Combined with BUG-31 the admin event screen is also reachable in the UI.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: PUT /api/events/{id} route handler has no admin guard (POST, DELETE and the other admin routes do)
bugs.hypothesis: The route is missing the role check the other admin routes share.
bugs.severityRationale: Critical: a customer can use an administrator-only operation that changes what every buyer sees (dates, venues), which the brief forbids "by any route". Rated on the accepted request; no real edit was sent, to protect the shared site.

bugs.title: A customer can cancel another customer's order
steps: Buyer A adds 1 Standard of event 7 and checks out; note order id N
Buyer B (a different fresh account) sends POST /api/orders/N/cancel
bugs.expected: B gets 403 or 404; A's order stays CONFIRMED
bugs.actual: B gets 200 and A's order is CANCELLED with a refund; order ids are sequential, so every order on the site can be cancelled
bugs.impact: Every buyer can lose their tickets to anyone; the business refunds orders nobody asked to cancel.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel loads the order by id without matching it to the session user
bugs.hypothesis: No order.userId === session.userId check.
bugs.severityRationale: Critical: any customer can destroy any other customer's purchase, and sequential ids make every order reachable. Harm to many buyers, no workaround for the victim.

bugs.title: A customer can read another customer's order, including recipient name and phone
steps: Buyer A checks out; note order id N
bugs.actual: 200 with A's recipientName, phone, studentCardNo and amounts; ids are sequential so all orders can be enumerated
bugs.impact: Every buyer: name, phone and student card number of any order are readable by any logged-in user, and ids are sequential, so every order can be enumerated. Same flaw as BUG-02, so the same severity.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: GET /api/orders/{id} loads the order by id without matching it to the session user
bugs.hypothesis: Same missing ownership check as BUG-02.
bugs.severityRationale: Critical: personal data (name, phone, student card) of every buyer is readable by any logged-in user through sequential ids. Same missing ownership check as BUG-02.

bugs.title: Adding 0 or a negative quantity to the cart is accepted, producing negative totals
steps: Log in as a fresh buyer
bugs.expected: Both adds rejected with 400 ("Each add is a whole number of at least 1"); cart empty. Removing a line with PATCH quantity 0 is a separate, legitimate action and is not part of this bug.
bugs.actual: Both return 200; the cart holds quantity -1 with gross -100,000, serviceFee -5,000, total -105,000
bugs.impact: Business: negative lines can offset other lines in the price. Checkout of a negative cart was deliberately not attempted, because it would change shared stock.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/cart/items body schema (quantity has no minimum); negative PATCH is already refused
bugs.hypothesis: The add schema allows any integer; PATCH refuses negatives, so only the add path is affected.
bugs.severityRationale: High: a stated booking rule is broken and the cart total goes negative; not Critical because checkout of a negative cart was not attempted, so the money effect is shown only in the cart.

bugs.title: The same discount code can be applied repeatedly and stacks
bugs.expected: The second apply is refused or ignored; discount stays 20,000; one code on the order
bugs.actual: discountCode becomes 'WELCOME10,WELCOME10,WELCOME10' and discount grows 20,000, 40,000, 60,000; the stacked discount is saved on the confirmed order
bugs.impact: Business revenue: any buyer can reach 100% off Standard tickets by repeating one request.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/cart/discount appends the code to a list instead of replacing or refusing
bugs.hypothesis: Codes are concatenated ("WELCOME10,WELCOME10") and each entry is applied.
bugs.severityRationale: Critical: direct revenue loss without limit; repeating one request reaches 100% off Standard tickets and the stacked discount is saved on the order.

bugs.title: Discount codes also reduce VIP and Student tickets
bugs.expected: discount 0, because codes apply to Standard tickets only; total 315,000
bugs.actual: discount 30,000 (10% of the VIP ticket); the same happens for Student tickets
bugs.impact: Business revenue on the highest-priced tickets.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: cart totals function applies the discount to the whole subtotal, not the Standard lines
bugs.hypothesis: No filter on ticket type before the discount is computed.
bugs.notes: The brief says "Discount codes apply to Standard tickets". I read that as Standard tickets only (GAP-09); if the product owner reads it otherwise, this bug and TC-DISC-04/05 change.
bugs.severityRationale: High: revenue lost on the most expensive tickets on every discounted VIP or Student line; rests on reading GAP-09 ("Standard only").

bugs.title: Service fee is charged on the subtotal before the discount
bugs.actual: discount 20,000; fee 10,000 (5% of 200,000); total 190,000. Same numbers in the cart UI and on the order
bugs.impact: Every buyer who uses a code is overcharged 5% of the discount; the brief calls this order of operations out explicitly.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: cart totals function computes the fee from gross instead of gross minus discount
bugs.hypothesis: fee = 5% × gross.
bugs.severityRationale: High: every buyer who uses a code is overcharged, and the brief states this order of operations explicitly ("on what is left after the discount"). Small per order but systematic, and it is the buyer's money.

bugs.title: VIP cap lets 5 VIP tickets into one order (off by one)
steps: Log in as a fresh buyer
POST /api/cart/items with 5 VIP tickets of event 7
bugs.expected: The fifth VIP is refused with 'An order may contain at most 4 VIP tickets'
bugs.actual: The add returns 200, the cart holds 5 VIP and the order is CONFIRMED with 5 VIP. The same fifth ticket is also accepted as 4 + 1, as 3 + 1 + 1 across two events, and by PATCH 4 to 5. Six is refused on every route.
bugs.impact: Business: VIP allocation rules are bypassed; scarce VIP stock goes to fewer buyers.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: VIP cap check on add and on PATCH
bugs.hypothesis: Observed: 5 accepted, 6 refused on every route, so the comparison allows one more than the cap (for example > 5 instead of > 4).

bugs.title: Past events can be booked through the API
steps: POST /api/cart/items with its Standard ticket type
bugs.expected: The add or the checkout is refused
bugs.actual: Both succeed; order CONFIRMED for an event that ended on 15 Aug 2026. The UI hides the Add buttons, so only the server check is missing
bugs.impact: Buyers pay for an event that already happened; refunds and complaints follow.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/cart/items and POST /api/orders do not check event status
bugs.hypothesis: The UI hides Add for past events; the server never checks.
bugs.severityRationale: High: buyers are charged for an event that has already happened; the UI hides it, so only direct API callers are affected today.

bugs.title: Cancelling after the event started refunds 100% instead of 0%
steps: Book the past event 11 through the API (only possible because of BUG-09)
Click Cancel tickets on that order
bugs.expected: refundAmount 0 ("After the start: 0%")
bugs.actual: refundAmount equals the full totalAmount (e.g. 420,000 of 420,000)
bugs.impact: Business revenue: every post-event cancellation is fully refunded. The 50% tier could not be tested (GAP-08).
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: refund-tier function (cancel handler)
bugs.hypothesis: Refund appears to be 100% whatever the time to start; the 0% tier is never reached.
bugs.notes: Depends on BUG-09 for its only reproduction. The real-world scenario (booked before the start, cancelled after it) needs an event that starts during the test; only an administrator can create one. Once BUG-09 is fixed, re-test with such a fixture before closing.
bugs.severityRationale: High: every post-start cancellation is refunded in full, against a stated refund rule; depends on BUG-09 for its only reproduction.

bugs.title: A cancelled order can be cancelled again, and each cancel returns its tickets to stock again
steps: Buy 1 Standard ticket of a quiet event and note remaining R after the purchase
Cancel the order: remaining returns to R + 1
bugs.expected: The second cancel is refused (4xx) and remaining stays at R + 1
bugs.actual: The second cancel returns 200 and remaining rises by 1 again, to R + 2. Each extra cancel adds the order's quantity once more, so stock grows past the event's capacity. The recorded run shows the exact numbers.
bugs.impact: Organiser and buyers: stock inflates past capacity, so the event oversells.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel has no CONFIRMED check before restocking
bugs.hypothesis: Cancel restocks unconditionally. The UI offers the button on cancelled orders too (BUG-36).
bugs.severityRationale: High: stock grows past capacity with each repeated cancel, so the event can oversell; reachable in one click through BUG-36.

bugs.title: Checkout still succeeds after the 10 minute cart hold has lapsed
steps: Add 1 Standard; note holdExpiresAt (add time + 10 min)
Wait 11 minutes without touching the cart
bugs.expected: Checkout refused until the cart is refreshed
bugs.actual: Order CONFIRMED 11 minutes after the last add; GET /api/cart still shows the lapsed holdExpiresAt
bugs.impact: Buyers can check out a cart whose hold has expired, at the prices and stock of more than 10 minutes earlier. Whether expired holds keep stock reserved from other buyers was not measured.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/orders does not compare now with cart.holdExpiresAt
bugs.hypothesis: holdExpiresAt is computed and returned but never enforced.

bugs.title: Sessions do not expire after 30 minutes
steps: Log in; the token's exp is iat + 1800 s
bugs.expected: 401; a fresh login is needed
bugs.actual: 200 for both 31 minutes later: the expiry in the token is not enforced
bugs.impact: Every buyer on a shared device: an abandoned session stays usable; a leaked cookie never ages out.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: session middleware verifies the token signature but not exp
bugs.hypothesis: The token carries exp = iat + 1800 s; requests after exp are still accepted.
bugs.severityRationale: High: a stated security rule (30-minute expiry) is not enforced, so an abandoned or leaked session stays usable indefinitely.

bugs.title: Recipient names over 50 characters are silently truncated instead of refused
bugs.expected: 400 naming the 50 character limit. The brief says the buyer "supplies a recipient name of at most 50 characters": a longer name must be refused, not changed.
bugs.actual: 200; the stored name is cut to 50 characters without telling the buyer
bugs.impact: Buyer: the ticket carries a name that is not the one entered.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/orders schema (recipientName)
bugs.hypothesis: The value is cut to 50 characters instead of being refused.

bugs.title: Checkout accepts phone numbers with fewer than 10 digits or no digits
bugs.expected: 400 for both
bugs.actual: 200 for both; orders are confirmed with unusable contact numbers
bugs.impact: Organiser cannot contact the buyer about changes or cancellations.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/orders schema (phone has no length or digit rule)
bugs.hypothesis: Neither length nor character class is checked at checkout.

bugs.title: Checkout accepts a blank recipient name
bugs.expected: 400. The brief only says "at most 50 characters"; treating a name of spaces as empty is my reading (GAP-07), stated so it can be challenged.
bugs.actual: 200; order confirmed for recipient ' '
bugs.impact: Door staff cannot match the ticket to a person.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/orders schema (recipientName not trimmed)
bugs.hypothesis: Only minLength 1 is checked, and spaces count.

bugs.title: Registration accepts malformed email addresses
steps: Repeat with 'qa-<something new>@@example.invalid' (two @ signs) and 'a<something new>@b' (no dot in the domain)
bugs.expected: 400 for each
bugs.actual: 200 for each; accounts are created with unusable identities
bugs.impact: Administrators resetting passwords cannot reach the user; junk accounts accumulate.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/auth/register schema (email is a plain string)
bugs.hypothesis: The OpenAPI schema declares email as type string with no format.
bugs.notes: Use a value nobody has registered yet: the bare 'not-an-email', 'qa@@example.invalid' and 'a@b' were registered by earlier runs (this bug), so they now answer 409 'Email already registered' instead of 200.

bugs.title: Phone numbers made of letters are accepted at registration and in the profile
bugs.expected: 400: only 10 to 15 digits
bugs.actual: 200 for both: only the length is checked, not that the characters are digits
bugs.impact: Contact data is unusable.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: register and PATCH /api/profile schemas (phone)
bugs.hypothesis: Only minLength 10 / maxLength 15 are declared in the OpenAPI schema; no digit pattern.

bugs.title: The same email can register a second account by adding a leading space
bugs.expected: 409 ("One email can register only one account"), as the same address in upper case already gets
bugs.actual: 200: a second account with ' E' is created; upper-case variants are correctly refused, so only whitespace is missed
bugs.impact: Breaks one account per email; lets one person bypass per-account limits.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: register handler (email not trimmed before the uniqueness check)
bugs.hypothesis: Case is folded before the check, whitespace is not.

bugs.title: New password equal to the current one is accepted
bugs.expected: 400: the new password must differ
bugs.actual: 200 'Password changed'
bugs.impact: Password rotation can be faked; the rule in the brief is not enforced. The UI hint says 'not the current one'.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: POST /api/profile/password (no comparison of new with current)
bugs.hypothesis: The current password is verified, then the new one is saved without comparing.

bugs.title: Search only matches the start of the event name: 'rock' finds nothing
bugs.expected: 'Hanoi Rock Fest' is listed (the brief's own example)
bugs.actual: 0 events. 'hanoi rock' finds it, 'fest' finds nothing (case is correctly ignored)
bugs.impact: Buyers cannot find events by the words they remember; direct lost sales.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: GET /api/events search filter
bugs.hypothesis: Observed: "hanoi rock" finds the event, "rock" and "fest" do not, so the filter matches the start of the title only (for example LIKE q%).
bugs.severityRationale: High: the brief's own example ("rock" returns Hanoi Rock Fest) fails; buyers cannot find events by the words they remember, which loses sales directly.

bugs.title: Search treats % and _ as wildcards and returns every event
bugs.expected: 0 results. The brief: "The search box matches any part of the event name"; no title contains % or _.
bugs.actual: All 23 events
bugs.impact: Minor for buyers; a sign that user text reaches the query as a pattern.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: GET /api/events search filter
bugs.hypothesis: % and _ return every event, consistent with the text being used as a LIKE pattern without escaping.

bugs.title: Sort by name sorts each page on its own, not the whole list
steps: Read the first card, then go to page 2
bugs.expected: Page 1 opens with 'Autumn Symphony Night', the first title of the whole list
bugs.actual: Page 1 opens with "Bat Trang Pottery Workshop"; "Autumn Symphony Night" (the first title of the whole list) is on page 2. The API returns the same order, so the defect is on the server.
bugs.impact: Buyers browsing alphabetically miss events.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: GET /api/events applies the title sort after LIMIT/OFFSET
bugs.hypothesis: Observed on the API: sort=title page 1 returns ids 1 to 10 sorted, page 2 ids 10 to 19, page 3 ids 20 to 23. The server takes the id-order slice first and sorts it afterwards; id 10 appearing on two pages is BUG-24.

bugs.title: Paging repeats the last event of each page at the top of the next page
steps: Note the last card of page 1
bugs.expected: Page 2 starts with the 11th event; 23 events over 3 pages without repeats
bugs.actual: 'Mui Ne Kitesurf Open' ends page 1 and starts page 2; 24 rows for 23 events
bugs.impact: Buyers see duplicates; with more events the error compounds across pages.
bugs.likelyLocation: Server: GET /api/events offset computation
bugs.hypothesis: Page p starts at index (p-1)*10-1 for p>1 (fits pages 2 and 3), so each page repeats the previous page's last event.

bugs.title: At 360 px the quantity field and Add button are off screen, so tickets cannot be bought on a phone
steps: Open an upcoming event on a 360 px wide phone screen
bugs.expected: Quantity and Add are visible and usable without zoom or sideways scrolling
bugs.actual: The card clips its contents: price is cut off, quantity starts at x=428 and Add at x=585, beyond the 360 px screen. Page scrollWidth stays 360, so the controls cannot be reached at all
bugs.impact: Every buyer on a phone: the purchase flow cannot be completed at 360 px, which the brief names explicitly.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: event detail ticket list (class "ticket-list is-tabular", flag f31)
bugs.hypothesis: A fixed 4-column grid (11rem 8rem 9rem 9rem) with overflow hidden cannot fit 360 px.
bugs.severityRationale: Critical: on a 360 px phone the buyer cannot reach quantity or Add, so the core purchase is impossible on the device class the brief names explicitly.
bugs.notes: Confirmed on a real iPhone 15 Pro Max and in the browser's phone emulation. Also reproduced on WebKit with the iPhone 13 profile (project mobile-webkit).

bugs.title: Profile screen scrolls sideways at 360 px when the email has no break point
bugs.expected: No sideways scroll
bugs.actual: scrollWidth about 490 px with a 41-character address such as nguyenvananh1790...@example.invalid; short hyphenated addresses wrap and hide the defect.
bugs.impact: Phone users with ordinary email addresses.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: profile email line (no overflow-wrap)
bugs.hypothesis: Long unbroken email text does not wrap.
bugs.notes: Also reproduced on a second engine: WebKit with the iPhone 13 profile (project mobile-webkit). Not yet checked on a real phone.

bugs.title: Event detail shows the UTC date and no time, not Vietnam time
bugs.expected: 5 Oct 2026, 00:30 (Vietnam time), as the list card correctly shows ('10/5/26, 12:30 AM')
bugs.actual: '2026-10-04': the UTC date, one day early, with no time
bugs.impact: Buyers of late-evening events plan for the wrong day; the detail page is where they decide.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: event detail start line (flag f24)
bugs.hypothesis: Bundle: new Date(startsAt).toISOString().slice(0,10) instead of the Vietnam-time formatter the list uses.
bugs.severityRationale: High: the detail page, where buyers decide, shows the day before for evening events after 17:00 UTC, so buyers can plan for the wrong day.

bugs.title: Checkout 'Phone number' label focuses the recipient field
bugs.expected: Cursor in the phone field
bugs.actual: Cursor in the recipient name field: the label has for='checkout-recipient'
bugs.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users; everyone who clicks labels.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: checkout form (flag f32)
bugs.hypothesis: Bundle: the Phone label htmlFor is "checkout-recipient" when f32 is on.

bugs.title: Search, discount code and cart quantity fields have no visible label
steps: Look for a label on the search box, the discount code field and the quantity field
bugs.expected: Every form field has a visible label that focuses it
bugs.actual: Placeholder or aria-label only; nothing to click
bugs.impact: Accessibility; the brief requires a visible label on every field.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: event list search box, cart discount field, cart quantity field
bugs.hypothesis: These inputs use placeholder or aria-label only; no <label>.

bugs.title: Order confirmation shows the total as a bare number
bugs.expected: Total formatted like the other lines, e.g. '₫210,000'
bugs.actual: Total reads '210000' while Service fee reads '₫10,000'
bugs.impact: Buyers misread the amount they paid.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: order confirmation total (flag f03)
bugs.hypothesis: Bundle: String(totalAmount) instead of the currency formatter used on the other lines.

bugs.title: Admin event screen renders for a customer, with Create and edit controls
bugs.expected: Access refused or redirected; no admin controls
bugs.actual: The admin events screen renders with its Create button. The API refuses create and delete, but edit is open (BUG-01), so this is a working UI route to it. No edit was submitted.
bugs.impact: Makes BUG-01 reachable without any tooling.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: /admin/events route renders without a role check
bugs.hypothesis: The client route is not guarded; the API refuses create and delete but not edit (BUG-01).

bugs.title: Next stays enabled on the last page and opens an empty 'page 4 of 3'
bugs.expected: Next is disabled on the last page
bugs.actual: Next is enabled; clicking it shows 0 events and the footer reads '23 events — page 4 of 3'
bugs.impact: Buyers paging through the list reach an empty page and may think events are missing.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: events list pager (flag f34)
bugs.hypothesis: Bundle: disabled when page > totalPages instead of page >= totalPages.

bugs.title: 'Added to cart' stays on screen next to the error of a later failed add
steps: Open an upcoming event while logged in
bugs.expected: Only the VIP error is shown: 'Messages on screen describe the result of the most recent action'
bugs.actual: 'Added to cart — view cart' is still shown together with 'An order may contain at most 4 VIP tickets'
bugs.impact: Buyers are told the last add succeeded when it failed.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: event detail add handler (flag f35)
bugs.hypothesis: Bundle: the success message is not cleared before a new add when f35 is on.

bugs.title: Removing the last cart line leaves the old total on screen
steps: Set the line quantity to 0 and leave the field
bugs.expected: The cart shows it is empty and the total reads ₫0
bugs.actual: The empty-cart message appears but the order summary still shows Total ₫105,000; the API returns total 0
bugs.impact: Buyers see an amount that no longer matches their cart.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: cart quantity handler (flag f01)
bugs.hypothesis: Bundle: on quantity 0 only the items are replaced from the response, not the totals.

bugs.title: Cart line names are clipped, hiding which ticket type each line is
steps: Add 1 Standard and 1 VIP ticket of the same event
Open the cart on a desktop screen
bugs.expected: Each line shows the event and the ticket type, e.g. 'Mid-Autumn Lantern Night — VIP'
bugs.actual: Both lines read 'Mid-Autumn Lant…'; the text is cut at 144 px of its 242 px, so the ticket type is never visible
bugs.impact: Buyers cannot tell their Standard and VIP lines apart before paying.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: cart line name (class 'line-name is-clamped', flag f33)
bugs.hypothesis: CSS: max-width 9rem with nowrap and ellipsis.

bugs.title: My orders offers 'Cancel tickets' on orders that are already cancelled
steps: Buy 1 ticket and cancel the order
bugs.expected: No cancel button on a CANCELLED order
bugs.actual: The CANCELLED order still shows 'Cancel tickets'; clicking it cancels again and returns stock again (BUG-11)
bugs.impact: Gives every buyer a one-click route to BUG-11's stock inflation.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: my orders row actions (flag f04)
bugs.hypothesis: Bundle: the button renders when f04 is on regardless of status.

bugs.title: On a phone, the opened menu is hidden behind the page, so a visitor cannot reach Log in or Sign up
steps: Open the site on a 360 px screen without logging in
bugs.expected: The login screen opens (and, once logged in, Cart, My orders and Profile in the menu can be tapped)
bugs.actual: The menu panel opens under the page: at the centre of Log in the topmost element is the page title 'Events', so the tap lands on the title and nothing happens. The same holds at every width below 1024 px (360 to 820 px checked), on Chromium and on WebKit (iPhone 15 Pro Max profile). No other screen links to login: the event detail, cart and orders screens have none, and Sign up exists only on the login screen. Logged in, Cart, My orders and Profile in the menu are covered the same way
bugs.impact: Every visitor on a phone or tablet in portrait: they cannot log in or register, so they cannot buy at all; logged-in buyers cannot reach the cart, their orders or their profile from the menu.
bugs.likelyLocation: Frontend: app header (class 'app-header is-flat' sets z-index auto, flag f30)
bugs.hypothesis: CSS: z-index auto lets page content stack above the header's menu panel.
bugs.severityRationale: Critical: below 1024 px a visitor who is not logged in has no tappable route to Log in or Sign up, so no purchase can start on a phone. The only way in is typing /login into the address bar, which an ordinary buyer would not know, so it is not counted as a workaround. Raised from High after the logged-out case was checked (the first report covered logged-in buyers only).
bugs.notes: Confirmed on a real iPhone 15 Pro Max and in the browser's phone emulation, logged out and logged in. Also reproduced on WebKit with the iPhone 13 and iPhone 15 Pro Max profiles.

observations.text: Changing the password does not end other sessions of the same account (GAP-06). Not a stated rule, raised as a question.

/api/config publishes 40 enabled flags (f01 to f65). Ten of them (f01, f03, f04, f24, f30, f31, f32, f33, f34, f35) appear in the frontend bundle, each switching a UI defect on; each UI bug names its flag. The others are presumably server-side; without the server source they are not mapped.
The cart accepts more tickets than remain in stock (100,000 Standard). Checkout was not attempted, to avoid draining shared stock (GAP-05).
Discount codes are accepted in any letter case and on an empty cart. The brief is silent; noted, not filed.

POST /api/events validates the body before it checks the role: a customer sending an incomplete body gets 400 with the admin schema's field list instead of 403. Nothing is created, so it is not a breach of the brief, but it discloses the admin API shape to customers.

effortNote: Effort (S/M/L) is my estimate from the observed behaviour, without the source code.
